title: Clearance-gated heading frame with contact-factorized conditioning
coverage_gap: A2 is the q3 winner at 0.900 but its remaining failures are confined to the HL cell: C 8/10 and E 3/5, versus perfect other reported cells. A1 fails both E cross-sign cells despite succeeding on both matched-sign E cells. These aggregate results motivate a directional transport-generalization hypothesis, not a confirmed diagnosis of the truncations. No failed-episode state or contact trace was supplied. The revised model tests an action-frame bias specifically after the object is raised, while preserving A2's successful reach/lift/carry factorization.
reusable_regularity: An elevated carried object can be transported in coordinates whose positive local y points toward the goal, whereas descent and grasp should retain native world axes and fixed gripper anisotropy. Use a smooth, observed-clearance gate on a horizontal yaw frame: exactly identity at or below wall top, transitioning over 0.08 m above it. This is a coordinate transform, not an action prescription or a collision-free planner. All actions still come from the one common diffusion U-Net. The same causal frame rotates relation vectors and translational action channels consistently. The independent learned behavioral phase gate from A2 remains observation-only and is trained with the same small auxiliary cross entropy.
dependencies_preserved: A2's reach/lift/carry branches, dimensions, 17-feature native-world causal phase input, positive gating floor and phase-label rule are retained. Reach/lift do not directly receive goal edges; carry does. At low object height the frame is exactly native-world identity.

The DP condition expands from 142 to 144 features solely to include frame cosine/sine. Absolute hand and wall centers, world object quaternions, both apertures and native increments preserve robot pose, workspace and fixed gripper orientation.

World-axis wall half-sizes and all twelve hand/object face distances stay unrotated. Top clearance and gate y/vertical motion remain world-axis quantities. Rotated vector edges plus explicit orientation retain the obstacle orientation rather than treating the finite box or robot as yaw invariant.

Current and native-previous hand/object relations and motion all use the identical chunk-start frame. Goal height stays in carry relations and the phase gate. Only declared absent object2 fields are unused.

No learned modules, losses, update counts, scheduler settings or control semantics outside the allowed candidate representation and invertible action frame are changed. Four diffusion channels only; no future joint channels, action filter, direct controller or additional DP.

evidence_refs.use: A2 scores 0.900 versus A3 0.775 and A1 0.525 under the fixed rule. A2's four failures are HL truncations only; A3 also reaches C=0.9 but has E=0.65 and latency about 0.191 s versus A2 about 0.107 s. Keep A2 architecture/loss and try a contact-protected frame without A3 joint diffusion. The comparison does not causally isolate frame from auxiliary-target effects.
A2 selected by equal-weight C/E score before implementing this one revision.
Actual code parent: three branch MLPs, learned causal phase gate, positive floor and phase auxiliary loss.
Actual conceptual/code parent for consistent chunk-start frame transforms. Do not inherit joint future channels or the always-goal-aligned frame.
Same exact D10 evidence; no additional demonstrations or other-session data.
Independent object/goal x factors, shared wall center/half-size, fixed world axes, native 0.01 m action scale and independent gripper.
Matched-sign support has small goal-object x offsets. Public observed wall top is about 0.12 m in these episodes.
Actual low grasp posture motivates protecting the world-frame grasp geometry.
Actual elevated object before transport motivates a clearance-gated frame rather than a goal frame at all stages.
Actual raised transport posture over the finite wall inspected.

Object starts near table, then is around 0.23-0.25 m high during world-y transport above the 0.12 m wall top. The 0.08 m clearance ramp reaches full orientation before this observed carrying regime without moving the low grasp frame. No threshold was fitted on development states.
Causal chunk-fixed encode/decode and independently masked nonnegative auxiliary objective.

expected_failure_signature: Directional hypothesis: improvement should be concentrated in HL transport-related generalization while already successful cells remain strong. If HL truncations come from grasp/contact or asymmetric robot/wall mechanics instead, this frame may not improve them at all. No physical failure subtype is claimed as observed.
An elevated but poorly attached object still activates the clearance frame; height is not contact truth. Rotation may amplify slips or incorrectly generalize a world-y command into a lateral motion.

The smooth transition can create changing local action coordinates over successive chunks during ascent or descent. Chunk-internal rotation is fixed, but poorly learned transitions may cause lateral hesitation or jitter.

The goal-heading regularization uses an 0.08 m minimum forward component to avoid near-goal yaw instability. Very short/behind-goal displacements are not fully aligned and can still undershoot or stall.

Native gripper and finite wall geometry break exact yaw symmetry. Despite retaining orientation and face distances, cross-sign E orientations lie outside much of support and may cause worse collisions or reaching behavior. A4 can underperform A2; q4 must retain the negative result if so.

required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,45] and raw_current [B,45] only. No external state, IDs, timestep, environment handles, future labels or oracle phase.
required_runtime_fields.frame_definition: Using raw_current only, top=wall_z+half_z, u=clamp((object_z-top)/0.08,0,1), weight=u*u*(3-2*u), d=goal_xy-object_xy. yaw=weight*atan2(-d_x,max(d_y,0.08)). Let c=cos(yaw), s=sin(yaw), R columns (c,s,0),(-s,c,0),(0,0,1). This is exactly identity for object_z<=top and tends to local +y goal alignment for an elevated object and d_y>=0.08. The clamp is on a geometric frame descriptor, never on actions. Both history observations and all sixteen action offsets use this one frame.
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: encode translation=R^T*native_delta_xyz; decode translation=R*encoded_delta_xyz. Gripper is unchanged and still drives [g,-g], xyz retains 0.01 m native scale and fixed native orientation. No candidate clipping or vector translation/rescaling. Only host clips decoded world actions and executes four of sixteen.
required_runtime_fields.scaling: Retains A2 metric relations 0.1 m, native-previous increments 0.01 m and absolute hand/wall centers 0.5 m. Frame ramp and heading floor are fixed geometric architecture choices, not support statistics or control gains.

training_only_targets.name: phase_labels
training_only_targets.source_fields: Same as A2: exact D_N support actions[step,1:3] and obs[step,5:7], wall center[40:42], half-size[43:45] for step=t and max(0,t-1).
training_only_targets.definition: 1 if native action_z>0.5 and abs(native action_y)<0.2; otherwise 2 if object_z>wall_top or object_y>wall_far_face; otherwise 0. Labels use original world actions, not rotated actions. They are coarse behavioral pseudo-labels, not oracle grasp/contact.
training_only_targets.loss: Unchanged 0.1*cross_entropy of two history stage logits, weighted by mask[:,0] for each history element and divided by max(1,2*sum(mask[:,0])). The common action4 epsilon loss remains weight 1 with denominator mask.sum()*4; no other auxiliary loss or future diffusion channel.
training_only_targets.inference_isolation: Only observation-predicted logits gate the encoders. Frame construction does not use predicted or true labels. No labels, targets or fitted support caches enter deployment.

support_fit: None. Training targets derive only from the current exact D_N. No optimizer updates or rollouts performed by the design/check loop.
change_summary: One feedback-driven scientific revision, trained from scratch in the A4 slot. Retain all A2 branch sizes, native-world phase features, gate floor, label rule and loss weight. Replace identity action frame and branch vector coordinates with a smooth clearance-gated, near-goal-regularized yaw frame; append two orientation features (condition 142 to 144). Use A3's consistent chunk-start encode/decode principle, but no always-on rotation and no joint future channels. A1-A3 remain immutable. No structural repairs as authored; no extra candidate or checkpoint search.
